title: Affine fppf acyclicity with only flat locally finitely presented comparison maps
statement:
Work in the universes and small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $U$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning a scheme isomorphic to the spectrum of a commutative ring [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. On its big fppf site $(\mathit{Sch}/U)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$ [def-pc-fppf-site], with structure sheaf $\mathcal O(v:V\to U)=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, let $G$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose its restriction to $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] is the associated etale sheaf $M_{\mathrm{et}}$ of a quasi-coherent Zariski $\mathcal O_U$-module $M$ [pqf-def-coherent], with $M_{\mathrm{et}}(v:V\to U)=\Gamma(V,v^*M)$ on etale objects. Suppose that for every flat, locally finitely presented $g:V\to U$ [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], the canonical comparison
$$g_{\mathrm{et}}^*(G|_{U_{\mathrm{et}}})\longrightarrow G|_{V_{\mathrm{et}}}$$
is an isomorphism; tensor pullback is [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then $H^q((\mathit{Sch}/U)_{\mathrm{fppf}},G)=0$ for all $q>0$. Here cohomology is the right derived functor of global sections in the category of structure-module sheaves, computed by injective module resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. There is no Noetherian, finite-generation, separation or comparison hypothesis for maps $V\to U$ that are not flat and locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 0756 (lemma-quasi-coherent-and-flat-base-change), with tau = etale and g = id_U, followed by affine quasi-coherent etale acyclicity (the affine vanishing application in stacks-sheaves.tex, section-change-topology).

proof.text: Put $A=A_U(M)$ using [lem-sfb-scheme-big-fppf-quasicoherent-equivalence], so $A(v)=\Gamma(V,v^*M)$. Let $\alpha:M_{\mathrm{et}}\xrightarrow{\sim}G|_{U_{\mathrm{et}}}$ be the given isomorphism. Restriction to opens gives $\beta:M\xrightarrow{\sim}\epsilon_{U,*}G$, since the inverse of the Zariski-etale equivalence is restriction to opens. The big-fppf-to-Zariski comparison identifies $A=\epsilon_U^*M$: its section presheaf is already a sheaf by the associated-sheaf equivalence. Under the ringed-topos module adjunction let $\varphi:A\to G$ be the adjunct of $\beta$. Thus there is a single morphism of big-site module sheaves, without assuming that $G$ is quasi-coherent on the whole big site.

source.place: Tag 0756 (lemma-quasi-coherent-and-flat-base-change), first two sentences of proof; Tag 070S (lemma-compare-sites)(1) and Tag 03FH (remark-change-topologies-ringed-sites)(1).

proof.text: For $g:V\to U$ flat and locally of finite presentation, the restriction of $\varphi$ to $V_{\mathrm{et}}$ is the composite $ (g^*M)_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq g_{\mathrm{et}}^*M_{\mathrm{et}}\xrightarrow{g_{\mathrm{et}}^*\alpha}g_{\mathrm{et}}^*(G|_{U_{\mathrm{et}}})\xrightarrow{c_g}G|_{V_{\mathrm{et}}}$. Here the first comparison is the pullback comparison in the Zariski-etale equivalence. To check the equality of maps, on an open $W\subset V$ both adjuncts send a section $m$ of $M$ on an open of $U$ containing $g(W)$ to its image under $\beta$, restricted along $W\to U$; tensor extension sends $a\otimes m$ to $a\,\beta(m)|_W$. This is the defining adjunct of the canonical comparison $c_g$. Naturality of the module adjunction and the identity-on-opens normalization therefore give the displayed equality. All three arrows are isomorphisms by the hypothesis on $c_g$. In particular $\varphi(V):A(V)\to G(V)$ is bijective.

source.place: Tag 0756 (lemma-quasi-coherent-and-flat-base-change), comparison map and its small-site restrictions; Tag 03FH (remark-change-topologies-ringed-sites)(2).

proof.text: Form $K=\ker\varphi$, $I=\operatorname{im}\varphi$ and $C=\operatorname{coker}\varphi$ in the abelian module-sheaf category. Kernels are sectionwise, so $K(V)=0$ on every flat locally finitely presented $V\to U$. For $C$, the quotient $G\to C$ is an epimorphism. Exact forgetting to abelian sheaves preserves this epimorphism, so local surjectivity gives, for any $s\in C(V)$, lifts $t_i\in G(V_i)$ on an fppf covering of $V$. Each $V_i\to U$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by composition, so $t_i$ is in the image of $\varphi(V_i)$ by step 2. Its image $s|_{V_i}$ in $C(V_i)$ is therefore zero. By the sheaf uniqueness axiom $s=0$. Thus $C(V)=0$ as well. Apply [lem-sfb-fppf-flat-lfp-zero-cohomology] to $K$ and $C$, at $\operatorname{id}_U$, to get $H^q(K)=H^q(C)=0$ for every $q\geq0$. The identity is flat and locally of finite presentation directly from the definitions.

source.place: Tag 0756 (lemma-quasi-coherent-and-flat-base-change), kernel and cokernel paragraph; Tag 0755 (lemma-cohomology-parasitic)(1).

proof.text: The chosen site is small in the common universe, so its module category is Grothendieck and has enough injectives by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] and [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Evaluation at $\operatorname{id}_U$ is additive and left exact, since kernels and finite products of module sheaves are sectionwise. Apply the long exact derived-functor sequence to $0\to K\to A\to I\to0$ and $0\to I\to G\to C\to0$. The first gives $H^q(A)\simeq H^q(I)$ because both adjacent groups $H^q(K)$ and $H^{q+1}(K)$ vanish; the second gives $H^q(I)\simeq H^q(G)$ because $H^{q-1}(C)$ and $H^q(C)$ vanish (in degree zero use the initial left-exact segment). Therefore $H^q(\varphi)$ is an isomorphism for every $q\geq0$. All these groups use injective module resolutions.

source.place: Tag 0756 (lemma-quasi-coherent-and-flat-base-change), the two short exact sequences; derived.tex Tag 015B (lemma-higher-derived-functors).

proof.text: For the associated sheaf $A=M^a$ on this affine $U$, [lem-sfb-affine-scheme-fppf-qcoh-acyclic] gives $H^q((\mathit{Sch}/U)_{\mathrm{fppf}},A_{ab})=0$ for $q>0$. The module/abelian evaluation comparison applies, using the small site, its commutative structure ring and the enough-injectives conclusion of step 4. It identifies this group with $H^q(A)$ computed in structure-module sheaves. Hence $H^q(A)=0$, and the isomorphism $H^q(\varphi)$ of step 4 proves $H^q(G)=0$ for all $q>0$. No comparison on any non-flat or non-locally-finitely-presented test map was used.
